Who Helps Mom and How to Reach Them

The family's contacts and care notes in one place: where each is kept, how recent it is, and what hasn't been collected yet.

Download PDF

Her doctor's number is in Mom's address book, the neighbor's is in your sister's phone, and nobody is sure where the notes from her last appointment went.

This page doesn't ask you to read or understand any of it. It asks who is involved, how to reach them, where each note is kept and how recent it is. Ask Mom before you copy anything of hers.

What to collectWhere it isIts dateWho has it
Mom's address and phone numbers
Family members: names and phone numbers
Neighbors and friends who help, and how to reach them
Her doctors and her pharmacy, with phone numbers
Other professionals or services she already uses
The list of who does what for her, if one has been written
Notes from her recent appointments
Other notes someone keeps: a calendar, a notebook, a list on the fridge
The family's own notes about her week
Mom's say-so to gather and share these: who asked her, and when

Scroll sideways to see every column, or print this page to fill it in.

What we haven't collected yet, and who will ask

Anything above with an empty line. Put a name next to each. There's no deadline.

For example Nobody has the pharmacy's number. Karen will ask Mom on Thursday.

How to use it

  • Ask Mom first. Her address book and her appointment notes are hers, and she decides what is shared and with whom.
  • Write the date on each note or list as you find it. If it has no date, write “undated.”
  • Don't copy out or summarize a note here. Just say where it is and who has it.
  • Tell the family where this page is kept.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't explain what any note or record means. If something in a note isn't clear, that's a question for the person who wrote it. An empty line is only something not collected yet.

Ready for the next step?

Where this comes from

Keeping one list of contacts for doctors and neighbors, with a column for where each thing is kept, follows AARP's Prepare to Care guide. The rows come from the Family Care Roadmap's working list for this step.
